subject.title: [Bug]: Browser interactions can exhaust model context by injecting too much page content

question: Should browser tool defaults move to compact goal-shaped reads and post-action change signals, or keep current capped snapshots with opt-in efficient mode?
rationale: The remaining work changes model-facing browser semantics and compatibility for existing full-snapshot workflows, so automation should not choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Adopt compact browser defaults
options.body: Make compact goal-shaped reads and small post-action change signals the default while preserving explicit full/raw snapshot access.

options.title: Keep capped snapshots
options.body: Retain the current AI snapshot caps and opt-in efficient mode, treating further compaction as targeted follow-up work.

options.title: Defer to broader compaction
options.body: Track this under broader context and tool-output compression architecture instead of browser-specific defaults.

recommendation.title: Adopt compact browser defaults
recommendation.body: Make compact goal-shaped reads and small post-action change signals the default while preserving explicit full/raw snapshot access.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about the browser plugin's public model-facing contract and history points most strongly to steipete for that boundary.
